data.name: issue_title
data.value: Pine live-edit loop: wrong plot values, compile adds the library, wizard writes the editor

data.name: stakeholder_overview
data.value:
Agents that update a published Pine library (reusable chart-indicator code) on TradingView Desktop currently get silently wrong plot numbers when they ask for a subset of series, can drop the library onto a live chart when they only meant to compile, and can type publish notes into the code editor because the generic fill tool misses the wizard field.

Those failures make a library update unsafe: the agent debugs the wrong values, pollutes a production layout, or nearly publishes wizard text as source. Closing the update wizard with the same Close control used for the editor can also raise a prompt that would delete the already-published library.

value.body:
## Summary

An agent walking a live Pine library update on TradingView Desktop received silently wrong indicator numbers, had the library dropped onto the chart, and twice nearly overwrote the library buffer with publish-wizard text. These are server-tool candidates from that walk. Follow-on to #26.

data.name: classification_rationale
data.value: The ticket names seven failing tool behaviours, each with a stated mechanism: filtered study-series reads index by the subset rather than full plot meta; smart compile prefers Add to chart over Pine Save on a library; generic input fill misses the library change-description placeholder and writes Monaco; wizard Close shares an aria-label with overlay Close and can raise Delete this publication; pine_bind loads the saved facade over unsaved edits; pine_publish reports an unchanged snapshot while an Update wizard is already open; chart-region screenshots capture covering overlays. That is specific restore-stated-behaviour work with cause known, not an inventive improvement. GitNexus impact on getStudySeries is LOW (three direct callers, two processes). The span is seven tools, so it is larger than a half-hour single-site fix and complexity is moderate rather than simple.

data.name: problem_statement
data.value:
TradingView MCP tools used in a live Pine library update currently fail in seven named ways. Filtered data_get_study_series reads assign later plot IDs the values of earlier slots because the in-page reader indexes the filtered ID list against full-meta row slots (an unfiltered RSIHeat read showed heatmap origin 110 under plot_9; the same IDs requested as plot_9–plot_18 returned RSI/band numbers). pine_smart_compile on an open library clicks Add to chart instead of Pine Save, then TradingView inserts the library as an extra study (RSIZones landed on a production layout that already had RSIHeat and RSIZGen). ui_set_input with the publish wizard open writes release notes into Monaco because the placeholder match misses “Describe the changes you made to your library” and falls back to the first visible field. Clicking Close by aria-label on an update draft raised Delete this publication. pine_bind loads the saved facade over a dirty buffer. pine_publish reported TV_PINE_PUBLISH_STALE while an Update library wizard was already on screen. A chart-region screenshot with the account sidebar open returned the menu, not the pane.

System: MCP stdio server over CDP to TradingView Desktop; tools in src/core/data.js (getStudySeries), src/tools/pine.js, UI input/click helpers, and capture. Impact: agents debug the wrong series, pollute live layouts, and can overwrite or delete a published library. Success is the ticket’s seven acceptance checks (filtered series values match unfiltered IDs; library compile persists without adding a study; wizard input cannot write Monaco; Close/delete prompts are classified; bind does not wipe a dirty buffer; publish does not stack wizards; chart capture does not accept an overlay clip). Constraints: Desktop CDP session, no TradingView API changes, private library already published (update-existing). Root cause of each trap is named in the ticket; application-script changes (RSIZones W membership, RSIHeat ribbon, RSIZGen latch) are out of scope.

data.name: stakeholder_overview
data.value:
Each of the seven traps gets a small, local fix in the tool that causes it: plot numbers are read from the right column, compiling a reusable library saves it without dropping it onto a live chart, publish notes go only into the notes field, Close buttons are told apart so a published library is not offered for deletion, unsaved editor text is kept unless the agent asks to reload, an already-open publish window is continued rather than opened twice, and a screenshot of the chart is refused when a menu is covering it.

That keeps a routine library update safe to run unattended: the agent sees the real plot values, does not pollute a production layout, and cannot overwrite or delete a published library by clicking the wrong Close or filling the wrong box.
